prompt: A ketone with a γ-hydrogen often shows a fragment at M-42 (loss of a C₃H₆ unit). What rearrangement explains this?

options.label: McLafferty rearrangement — γ-H migrates to C=O, α-β bond cleaves, releasing a neutral alkene
α-cleavage next to C=O, releasing an acyl radical and forming a resonance-stabilized cation
A retro-Diels-Alder, cleaving the enone framework into a diene and dienophile
Loss of CO₂ (decarboxylation), which contributes 44 mass units with a neutral radical loss

explanation: McLafferty: γ-H transfers to C=O oxygen (6-membered TS), α-β C-C bond cleaves, releasing a neutral alkene. Loss of C₃H₆ = 42 Da (propene fragment). Diagnostic of ketones/aldehydes/esters with γ-H. α-cleavage (option b) also happens, but produces different mass losses (R group as radical).
